security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel saves/restores vtype CSR without preserving bits lambda[2:0] (vtype[XLEN-2:XLEN-4]), altfmt_A (vtype[9]), altfmt_B (vtype[10]), or bs (vtype[11]) across context switch, trap handling, or signal delivery, causing these Zvvm-defined fields to be clobbered to zero on any kernel entry/exit
security_spec.summary: Zvvm adds 6 new bits to vtype CSR (lambda[2:0] at high bits, altfmt_A/B at bits 9-10, bs at bit 11) controlling matrix tile geometry and microscaling; kernel vtype save/restore paths must preserve these bits or userspace IME context is silently corrupted across context switches

findings.finding: vtype CSR restoration uses 'vsetvl x0, %2, %1' (line 172) which per RISC-V spec only writes standard vtype fields (VSEW[5:3], VLMUL[2:0], VTA[6], VMA[7], VILL[XLEN-1]). Bits [8] through [XLEN-2], where Zvvm defines lambda[2:0] (vtype[XLEN-2:XLEN-4]), altfmt_A (vtype[9]), altfmt_B (vtype[10]), and bs (vtype[11]), are NOT written by vsetvl and get zeroed on any kernel entry/exit. No Zvvm hardware exists today so no actual data corruption occurs, but the save/restore infrastructure is architecturally incapable of preserving tile format state.
findings.snippet:
asm volatile (
	".option push\n\t"
	".option arch, +zve32x\n\t"
	"vsetvl	 x0, %2, %1\n\t"
	".option pop\n\t"
	"csrw	" __stringify(CSR_VSTART) ", %0\n\t"
	: : "r" (src->vstart), "r" (src->vtype), "r" (src->vl));

findings.finding: Save path executes 'vsetvli %0, x0, e8, m8, ta, ma' (line 219) for vector register data transfer BEFORE the vtype save happens. While __vstate_csr_save is called first and reads the full vtype CSR including Zvvm bits, the subsequent vsetvli clobbers Zvvm tile format bits in hardware vtype CSR to zero. The in-memory save_to->vtype correctly captures tile bits, but hardware vtype state is destroyed here even on the save side.
findings.snippet:
"vsetvli	%0, x0, e8, m8, ta, ma
	"
"vse8.v		v0, (%1)
	"
"add		%1, %1, %0
	"
"vse8.v		v8, (%1)
	"

findings.finding: Restore path first runs 'vsetvli %0, x0, e8, m8, ta, ma' (line 255) for VLE8.V data transfer which zeros Zvvm tile bits in hardware vtype before __vstate_csr_restore attempts to restore vtype via vsetvl. Combined with the vsetvl limitation in __vstate_csr_restore, this means Zvvm tile format bits are doubly clobbered (first by vsetvli for data transfer, then vsetvl cannot write them back).
findings.snippet:
"vsetvli	%0, x0, e8, m8, ta, ma
	"
"vle8.v		v0, (%1)
	"
"add		%1, %1, %0
	"
"vle8.v		v8, (%1)
	"

findings.finding: Save correctly reads full vtype CSR via 'csrr %1, CSR_VTYPE' (line 133) which captures all bits including Zvvm tile fields lambda[2:0], altfmt_A, altfmt_B, bs into dest->vtype. The in-memory snapshot is complete.

Ptrace vtype validation mask 'reserved = ~(VTYPE_VSEW | VTYPE_VLMUL | VTYPE_VMA | VTYPE_VTA)' (line 150) correctly rejects writes to bits [8] through [XLEN-1] (except VILL). While this means a Zvvm-aware ptracer cannot set tile format bits, this is defensive since the kernel cannot restore those bits anyway. The mask should be relaxed only alongside a proper save/restore fix.

KVM VCPU vector save/restore delegates to __kvm_riscv_vector_save/__kvm_riscv_vector_restore, which directly call __riscv_v_vstate_save/__riscv_v_vstate_restore. Guest Zvvm tile format vtype bits will be zeroed on VM exit (save path) and cannot be restored on VM entry (restore path) due to the same vsetvl limitation.

Signal delivery calls riscv_v_vstate_save() (line 93) which saves vtype correctly to memory, then the vsetvli in __riscv_v_vstate_save clobbers hardware vtype tile bits. When the process resumes after signal handler returns, deferred restore via arch_exit_to_user_mode_prepare calls riscv_v_vstate_restore, which cannot restore Zvvm tile bits through vsetvl.

Deferred vector restore on return to userspace calls riscv_v_vstate_restore() (line 19) which invokes __vstate_csr_restore -> vsetvl. Any Zvvm tile format bits saved in current->thread.vstate.vtype will NOT be written back to hardware vtype CSR because vsetvl does not cover those bit positions.

Context-switch path calls riscv_v_vstate_save() on prev and riscv_v_vstate_set_restore() on next. The deferred restore mechanism (TIF_RISCV_V_DEFER_RESTORE) means next's vstate will be restored via arch_exit_to_user_mode_prepare -> vsetvl on return to userspace, which cannot restore Zvvm tile format bits. Affects both non-preemptive and CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_V_PREEMPTIVE paths.
